questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good university (modern and good ranking)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was okay. When I had questions I got fast answers. 
More information about housing benefits would have been nice (boligstøtte)
And I didn't no that also the intro week is included for the Erasmus legat. Would be nice to get more information about that befor the start.

questions.answer:
Student service in Wageningen
Tutors 
UCPH

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky, but in general it is very difficult to find accommodation in Wageningen

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They need to buy a bike directly hen arriving in Wageningen. It is a small city and public transport is very very bad.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: a lot of mails

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: asking UCPH

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: got all the classes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Level is higher than on KU. Periods of 6 week and not 8 but with the same amount of pensum.
Exam is more difficult --> all exams are without aids
All can only be passed with over 55% while it is over 50% on KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Bette, More practicals, better planning, web lectures, guest lectures in all classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Food digestion: Fermentation and gut health (Master)
Food Microbiology (Bachelor)
Pharmacology and nutrition (Bachelor)
Nutrition research methodologies (Master)
Design and interpretation of nutrition intervention studies (Master)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All my courses. Very good teachers and good planning. 
All were highly relevant but always choose courses which suits your interest

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
*I had only to buy one book (40euros/300dkk) all other literature and books where handed put as an pdf
 
Two time double rent because I already had my apartment in Wageningen from the 01.08.23 and also couldn't find someone to subvent my apartment in Denmark for January. 

Had to stay longer than my Erasmus legat --> due to resit for a eksam --> had to pay rent for the extra day 

** personal spending and spending on food are only a guess, I have no idea how much it was. But definitely less than in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Bike where more expensive then I thought. 200euros for a used one and 100euros for reparations 
Books where less expensive (didn't had to buy books)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good sports center on campus ! KU could learn a lot from Wageningen on this point

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
All kinds of sports (over 30) all at one play (sports center)
Very cheap to use the gym, swimming pool, squash, volleyball etc.  (80euros for one semester)
When joining a sportsclub 20euros for one semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
join a sports club
A lot of activity and you can socialise with other student, especially locals

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Wageningen is a very bad city to live in when you want a lot of non academic activity. Small city and I think 99% of the local student a going to their home citys in the weekends. 
Nearly all students left in Wageningen are international students 

Possible to go to Amsterdam or Utrecht
Neighbour city Ede have a cinema, jump park and minigolf and some other stuff

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Had most contact with other international students

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Join a sports club
Be active and socialise during group work during the classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
Food 
otherwise not much different from Denmark or Germany

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Plan a lot of time for studying and prepare. 
Join a sports club and socialise throw ESN directly upon arrival
Join the Intro week (AIDs )
Don't forget to visit other city like Amsterdam, Utrecht, Rotterdam etc.

questions.answer: none.
